change: reference model: global word TF-IDF (hashing) + classical linear models, small grid search
notes: frozen before any experiment; every experiment is compared against it

change: fine-tuned XLM-R base; trains on one random 512-token window per text per epoch, predicts by averaging all windows (per-language window cap)
notes: max_chunks from EDA token counts: p99 of windows per text is 8 for English and 4 for German

change: token-level XLM-R base: every token is tagged original / rewritten / ai, with labels from train fusion texts and their human source (a word is rewritten when none of its word 3-grams occurs in the source); per-text summaries of the token probabilities go to the stacker
notes: targets lightly rewritten fusion: X4 calls 44% of validation fusion texts with <= 5% rewritten words human. Fusion texts without a known source are left out of training; fusion training windows contain a rewritten token with probability `focus`; prediction covers the whole text with overlapping windows. Standalone scores: ai = mean ai probability, fusion = (1 - ai) * max of the `smooth`-token moving average of the rewritten probability

change: stacker trained on the train part: 5-fold group out-of-fold scores of the linear TF-IDF members over all train texts, plus the given domain and text stats, per-language gradient boosting; used as one input of the validation stacker X4
notes: the X4 stacker only has 27k validation rows (5k German); S1 learns how to combine the linear members on 245k rows. Val/test inputs are the members' usual full-train predictions. Member OOF scores are cached as preds/<member>_trainoof.parquet; delete them after re-running a member

change: one model per language with its own feature/regularisation search (cased words and char n-grams offered to German)
notes: motivated by EN/DE differences in EDA: German capitalises nouns, compounds words and has only two domains

change: two-stage: stage-1 domain classifier routes each text to a per-domain expert (same features and model as B0)
notes: domains have very different class priors and styles; domains below min_domain_docs fall back to the global model

change: two-stage with routing by the given domain column instead of the stage-1 prediction
notes: domains have very different class priors and styles; domains below min_domain_docs fall back to the global model

change: open-weight LM likelihood features (observer/performer log-probs, entropy, Binoculars ratio, spread over 64-token segments) + gradient boosting
notes: segment spread targets fusion (partly rewritten text); token budget per language from EDA: Qwen needs 1.85 tokens/word in German vs 1.23 in English

change: open-weight LM likelihood features (observer/performer log-probs, entropy, Binoculars ratio, spread over 64-token segments) + gradient boosting
notes: segment spread targets fusion (partly rewritten text); token budget per language from EDA: Qwen needs 1.85 tokens/word in German vs 1.23 in English

change: two-stage stacked ensemble: stage 1 diverse base models (word/char TF-IDF, per-language, per-domain, label cascade, sentence model, encoder, LM features); stage 2 per-language gradient-boosting stacker over their scores, the given domain, encoder window stats, LM and text-statistic features
notes: stacker is trained and scored with group k-fold inside the validation split (out-of-fold predictions), then refit on all validation rows for test

change: X4 plus per-language class offsets added to the stacker log-probabilities, tuned for macro-F1 by grid search
notes: offsets for each validation fold are tuned on the other folds' out-of-fold predictions, so the validation score stays out-of-sample; test uses offsets tuned on all validation rows

change: two-stage label cascade: stage 1 ai vs not-ai, stage 2 human-vs-fusion specialist trained only on human and fusion texts (B0 features and model)
notes: replaces domain routing as the two-stage idea (domain is given in test); B0's human/fusion boundaries also have to separate ai texts, the specialist only separates the hard pair

change: character n-grams (char_wb 3-5, cased, first 2000 characters) instead of word n-grams, small C search
notes: added as a diverse ensemble member: splits text differently from the word models; trained on a 120k subsample (11.2 GB peak, about 2 min; macro-F1 0.763 at 20k, 0.792 at 60k, 0.808 at 120k)

change: two-stage sentence model: stage 1 labels each sentence original / rewritten / ai (B0 features), trained on sentence labels derived from train fusion texts and their human source by word 3-gram overlap; stage 2 gradient boosting over per-text summaries of the sentence scores
notes: half of the train fusion texts have a human source (TF-IDF neighbour, cosine >= split link_threshold); their sentences are bimodal (about 77% copied unchanged, 15-23% fully rewritten). Stage 1 and stage 2 are fitted on disjoint train groups, so stage 2 sees sentence scores as on val/test

change: masked word n-grams (text distortion): the most frequent words of the training texts and punctuation are kept, every other word becomes '*' repeated to its length; word 1-3-gram TF-IDF + linear SVM, small search over the kept vocabulary and C
notes: a style/syntax member with almost no topic signal (Stamatatos 2017, text distortion); kept words are learned on the fitted training texts only, one shared list for EN and DE
